settings.paragraph_text: R95. 8cm tall, in cool enamel. For the long table outside, the picnic basket, the kitchen shelf people ask about.

settings.heading_text: The blikbeker is probably the most recognisable cup in South Africa.
settings.paragraph_text:
White enamel. Blue rim. The small dent on the side from years of camping, church bazaars and padkos. There was one in almost every kitchen.

Now there is a pink one too.

8cm tall — right for an espresso, a small dop, or a glass of bubbly when lunch runs long.

Cool enamel that holds its temperature. Made by Eersteklas, who have been making enamel cups in South Africa long enough that the blue-and-white version has become part of the country's kitchens.

The same cup. Just a different colour.

settings.heading_text: Maroelamark is for people who set their own table.
settings.paragraph_text: The shelf where old familiar things feel right again: Pa Wessel's coffee sack, Streepsak, Tafelstories, Eersteklas. Things people remember, just lighter, quieter and more at home in the kitchens of now. Not a homeware store. More the place you go to look when you want something for the table that does not feel like everybody else's.
settings.review_text: White enamel. Blue rim. The small dent on the side from years of camping, church bazaars and padkos. There was one in almost every kitchen.

settings.heading_text: A small pink cup on a lace tablecloth under the trees.
settings.paragraph_text: Two of them on a wooden tray between friends before lunch starts. Four on an open kitchen shelf — three white, one pink — and everybody immediately understands what they are looking at. A wedding table with one at every place setting. The picnic basket for Hermanus that somebody packed carefully because they wanted to. The blikbeker has moved from the camping cupboard to the table.
